gatekeepers: Customer Workspace admins (for domain-wide installs, only admins can allowlist the app)
summary.nextAction: Create a separate Google Cloud project for production and enable the Gmail API.

steps.title: Create a separate Google Cloud project for production
steps.detail: Google recommends separate projects for testing and production. Use the production project for everything below.

steps.title: Enable the Gmail API in that project
steps.detail: APIs & Services → Library → Gmail API → Enable.

blocker.symptom: Connections fail with 'Gmail API has not been used in project'
blocker.cause: The Gmail API is not enabled in the project that owns your OAuth client
blocker.fix: Enable the Gmail API in the same project, wait a few minutes, retry

steps.title: Set up branding and verify your domain
steps.detail: Add app name, support email, home page and a privacy policy hosted on the same domain as the home page. Verify the domain in Google Search Console. Personal Google accounts (no organisation) can only choose the External audience.

steps.title: Create the OAuth client and add Composio's redirect URI
steps.detail: Create a Web application OAuth client and add Composio's redirect URI. Leave "Use this client for an AI-powered agent" off unless you use Google's own MCP tools; Composio calls the Gmail API directly.

blocker.symptom: redirect_uri_mismatch right after creating the client
blocker.cause: Google says new client settings can take five minutes to a few hours to take effect
blocker.fix: Wait and retry before changing anything

steps.title: Declare the smallest scope that fits what your agent does
steps.detail: Replace Composio's default Gmail scopes: they include full mailbox access and nine personal-data scopes, which would trigger the strictest review. Add only the scope for your chosen capability (see Scopes) on Google's Data Access page and in your Composio auth config.

blocker.cause: The app requests a sensitive or restricted scope Google hasn't approved for it
blocker.fix: Request only declared, approved scopes; complete verification before requesting more

steps.title: Connect your app to Composio
steps.detail: Create a custom auth config with your client ID, secret and scopes, then pass its ID when creating sessions.

copyValues.label: Python

steps.title: Test it in the Composio Playground
steps.detail: Add yourself under Audience → Test users first. Then open the auth config, choose Connect Account, continue past "Google hasn't verified this app", and run one Gmail tool.

blocker.symptom: "Access blocked: composio.dev has not completed the Google verification process" (Error 403: access_denied)
blocker.cause: In Testing mode only listed test users can sign in, and your account isn't on the list
blocker.fix: Add the account under Audience → Test users, click Save, and check it appears in the list

steps.title: Check the granted scopes, not just the connection status
steps.detail: Google lets users untick permissions, so a connection can be active without Gmail access. After each connection, read the connected account's granted scopes; if the Gmail scope is missing, ask the user to reconnect and tick it, then remove the old connection.

blocker.symptom: Gmail tools fail with 403 "Request had insufficient authentication scopes"
blocker.cause: The user didn't grant the Gmail permission on Google's consent screen
blocker.fix: Send a new connect link and ask them to tick the Gmail permission

steps.title: Publish branding (brand verification)
steps.detail: Branding page → Verify Branding → Publish. Typically 2–3 business days if branding changed.

steps.title: Request data-access verification
steps.detail: In the Verification Center, justify each scope and upload an unlisted demo video showing the consent screen and how your app uses each scope.

blocker.cause: The verification wait only starts when you submit
blocker.fix: Submit as soon as branding and scopes are final, and request only the scopes your agent uses

steps.title: Pass the annual security assessment
steps.detail: Reading mail uses restricted scopes. Apps that access restricted data from or through a server need a third-party security assessment, repeated at least every 12 months. Send-only agents skip this.

blocker.symptom: Approval takes weeks longer than planned
blocker.cause: Restricted-scope verification and the security assessment can take several weeks
blocker.fix: Start early, or use send-only (gmail.send) if your agent doesn't need to read mail

steps.title: Remove the remaining Composio branding
steps.detail: Your own client changes Google's consent screen, but users still see composio.dev on Google's account chooser and "Composio wants to connect" on the Connect Link page. Brand the Connect Link in Project Settings → White Labeling and proxy the OAuth redirect through your own domain.

steps.title: Move existing users to your app
steps.detail: Users who connected through Composio's managed app stay on it until they reconnect. Ask them to reconnect once your app is approved.

unknowns: Whether Composio-hosted token storage counts as server access for Google's assessment rule (inferred yes; confirm with Composio).
Each Gmail scope's tier must be re-checked against Google's current list at build time.
Team audience: a personal Google account can't use the Internal user type (tested); Internal avoids review only if every user is in your own Workspace organisation.
Which name Google's consent screen itself shows when the redirect goes through composio.dev (we didn't capture that screen).
Whether verification accepts composio.dev as an authorised domain you don't own; proxying the redirect through your domain avoids the question.

evidence.label: official
evidence.claim: With Composio-managed apps, users see 'Composio wants to access your account'; production apps should show your own name.

evidence.label: official
evidence.claim: A common Gmail error is 'Gmail API has not been used in project' (API not enabled).
evidence.note: FAQ answer text did not load; cause stated from the error wording.

evidence.label: official
evidence.claim: Google can block sign-in ('App is blocked') when an app requests a sensitive or restricted scope not approved for it.
evidence.sourceTitle: Composio KB: Google OAuth setup and consent

evidence.label: official
evidence.claim: gmail.send is a sensitive scope and requires Google verification; https://mail.google.com/ is full mailbox access and broader than many customers want.

evidence.label: official
evidence.claim: Brand verification typically takes 2–3 business days; restricted-scope verification can take several weeks; apps accessing restricted data from or through a server need a security assessment at least every 12 months; testing apps show a warning screen, have a user cap and limited refresh-token lifetime; internal-only Workspace apps and personal use are exceptions; privacy policy must be on the home page's domain and domains verified.

evidence.label: official
evidence.claim: Google's verification FAQ holds the current list of sensitive and restricted scopes.
evidence.note: Re-check each Gmail scope's tier against this list at build time.

evidence.label: official
evidence.claim: Changing scopes affects new connections only; existing users keep granted scopes until they reconnect. Make sure your OAuth app has the scopes approved in the provider's portal.

evidence.label: official
evidence.claim: Existing connections keep refreshing with their original auth config; full migration means re-authentication (or import where supported). To remove Composio branding: set the Connect Link logo and title in Project Settings → White Labeling, use your own OAuth app for the consent screen, and proxy the OAuth redirect through your own domain so backend.composio.dev isn't shown.

evidence.label: official
evidence.claim: For OAuth toolkits, the Composio dashboard shows the redirect URI to add in the provider's developer portal.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.claim: Because Composio stores and refreshes users' tokens on its servers, a Composio-based Gmail integration likely counts as server access, so the security assessment applies to restricted scopes.
evidence.sourceTitle: Inference from Composio managed-auth docs + Google rule
evidence.note: Confirm with Composio before presenting as fact.

evidence.label: official
evidence.claim: Selecting Connect Account on an auth config authenticates the project's Playground user for testing.

evidence.label: tested
evidence.claim: We created a Google Cloud project on a personal Google account (no organisation): only the External audience was available. In Testing mode Google limits sign-in to listed test users and caps the app at 100 users over its lifetime before verification. With no test user saved, sign-in failed with "Access blocked: composio.dev has not completed the Google verification process" (Error 403: access_denied). Once added as a test user, Google showed "Google hasn't verified this app" with Back to safety highlighted and Continue as the secondary button.
evidence.sourceTitle: Our test: Google OAuth client in Testing mode via Composio (2026-10-23)

evidence.label: tested
evidence.claim: Creating a Web application client: Google adds the redirect URI's domain (composio.dev) to the consent screen's authorised domains, warns that settings can take five minutes to a few hours to take effect, and offers a "Use this client for an AI-powered agent" option described as being for clients that use Google MCP tools.
evidence.sourceTitle: Our test: Google Auth Platform client form (2026-10-23)

evidence.label: tested
evidence.claim: Composio's own-credentials form for Gmail pre-fills the redirect URI https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add and starts with 11 scopes, including https://mail.google.com/ (full mailbox, restricted) and nine People API scopes (contacts, addresses, birthday, phone numbers and others). We replaced them with userinfo.email and gmail.readonly.
evidence.sourceTitle: Our test: Composio Gmail auth config (2026-10-23)

evidence.label: tested
evidence.claim: Google's consent let the user grant only some scopes: the first connection went ACTIVE in Composio with userinfo.email and openid but not gmail.readonly, and the first Gmail tool call failed with 403 "Request had insufficient authentication scopes" (ACCESS_TOKEN_SCOPE_INSUFFICIENT). Reconnecting with the Gmail permission granted created a second connected account (the first stayed active); with it, a read-only profile lookup worked and the token came with a refresh token.
evidence.sourceTitle: Our test: connecting Gmail through Composio (2026-10-23)

evidence.label: tested
evidence.claim: Even with our own Google client, Google's account chooser said "to continue to composio.dev" (the redirect domain), and Composio's Connect Link page said "Composio wants to connect to your Gmail".
evidence.sourceTitle: Our test: what users see when connecting (2026-10-23)
